agent.problem: This stop relies on discovery questions more than informed guesses. Cards 2, 6, 8, 11, 15 and 18 ask for the firstborn, the dividing of the sea, Pharaoh's fate, the kings' names, when the LORD remembered us, and what He gives every creature without earlier cards providing a basis for choosing among the answers. Six of the ten choices therefore depend on prior knowledge or luck.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

human.problem: This card sits in stop 1 (Psalm 136:1-9) but cites Psalm 136:1-26, because it describes the refrain ending all 26 verses. The citation matches what the card uses, but it reaches well past its stop's range. The reveal screen after stop 1 shows only the verses covered so far.
human.question: Can a card cite verses beyond its own stop's range when it describes a pattern across the whole passage, like a refrain? Or should the citation be limited to the stop's verses, with the card worded to fit?
